assessment_summary: The proof correctly reduces the Hamiltonian Path problem to the LongPath17 problem by adding 17 isolated vertices to the original graph. The forward and backward implications are logically sound. Although there is a confused and strictly false intermediate sentence ('any set of n distinct vertices of G must include all the original vertices VH (and possibly some of the added ones)'), the proof does not actually rely on this claim. Instead, it correctly deduces that the path must be drawn entirely from VH because it is impossible for a multi-vertex path to include isolated vertices. Since |VH|=n, any such path must visit every vertex of H, making it a Hamiltonian path. The reduction is robust and the overall mathematical argument is valid.
